Let

\[ S = \sum_{k=0}^{2026} k \binom{2k}{k} 2^k. \]

Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(p=2027\). We work modulo \(p\).

First, for \(k>p/2\) and \(k<p\), the number \(2k\) contains the factor \(p\) while \(k!\) does not, so
\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p.
\]
Thus only \(0\le k\le (p-1)/2\) matter. For these \(k\),
\[
\binom{p-1-k}{k}
=\frac{(p-1-k)(p-2-k)\cdots(p-k)}{k!}
\equiv (-1)^k\frac{(k+1)(k+2)\cdots(2k)}{k!}
\equiv (-1)^k\binom{2k}{k}\pmod p.
\]
Hence
\[
S\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2} k(-2)^k\binom{p-1-k}{k}.
\]

Let
\[
G(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\binom{p-1-k}{k}x^k.
\]
Then \(S=xG'(x)\big|_{x=-2}\). Also
\[
G(x)=[t^{p-1}]\frac1{1-t-xt^2}.
\]
Differentiating,
\[
S\equiv -2[t^{p-3}]f(t)^2,
\qquad
f(t)=\frac1{1-t+2t^2}.
\]

Let \(r,s\) be roots of \(z^2-z+2=0\), so \(r+s=1,\ rs=2\). Put
\[
\Delta=r-s,\qquad D=\Delta^2=(r-s)^2=-7.
\]
For \(p=2027\),
\[
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)
=\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right).
\]
Since \(2027\equiv 3\pmod4\), the first factor is \(-1\). By quadratic reciprocity,
\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
= -\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
= -\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)
=-1.
\]
So \(-7\) is a quadratic residue mod \(2027\), and \(r,s\in\mathbb F_{2027}\).

Using
\[
f(t)=\frac{r}{\Delta}\frac1{1-rt}-\frac{s}{\Delta}\frac1{1-st},
\]
one obtains
\[
[t^N]f(t)^2
=
\frac{N+1}{D}\bigl(r^{N+2}+s^{N+2}\bigr)
-
\frac{4}{\Delta^3}\bigl(r^{N+1}-s^{N+1}\bigr).
\]
Take \(N=p-3\). Since \(r,s\in\mathbb F_p\),
\[
r^{p-1}=s^{p-1}=1,\qquad r^{p-2}=r^{-1},\ s^{p-2}=s^{-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
[t^{p-3}]f(t)^2
=
\frac{-2\cdot 2}{D}
-\frac{4}{\Delta^3}\left(\frac{s-r}{2}\right)
=
-\frac4D+\frac2D
=
-\frac2D.
\]
Therefore
\[
S\equiv -2\left(-\frac2D\right)=\frac4D
= \frac{4}{-7}\pmod{2027}.
\]
Since
\[
7\cdot 289=2023\equiv -4\pmod{2027},
\]
we have
\[
(-7)\cdot 289\equiv 4\pmod{2027}.
\]
So
\[
S\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
